key_insight: Sparse AFM scans can be expanded into a probabilistic microstructure ensemble that predicts distributions, not just single values, of plant cell wall stiffness and strength across scales.
engineering_relevance: This enables multiscale constitutive modeling of developing fiber walls when experiments are limited, supporting uncertainty-aware design and interpretation of biomaterial mechanics.
method: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion with LoRA to generate AFM-like wall microstructures from sparse scans.
Convert each synthetic microstructure into spatial Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio fields via an intensity-to-property mapping.
Run strain-controlled finite element homogenization and propagate effective properties into stochastic tensile simulations at the specimen scale.
evidence_signal: The workflow evaluates synthetic images using microfibril crossover count and crossover angle, then produces property and stress-response distributions over an image ensemble and stiffness-ratio sweep.
watch_item: Quantitative accuracy still depends on calibrating the image intensity-to-property mapping with nanomechanical measurements, so current results are methodological rather than fully predictive.
paper_title: From Sparse AFM Observations to Probabilistic Macroscale Mechanics: A Generative-Physics Framework for Plant Cell Walls
